done_when: Handing back an intake as a plan for an existing story key adds it to that story with no git error, or refuses before using the intake with a plain reason and next step

known.title: Preserve plan structure when appending intake requirements

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - extending an existing story with intervening sections or a saved design.
The joining path appends each field immediately before the named following heading, rather than within its owning section. For the supported layout in tests/test_story.py:36–50 (`Done when`, then `Tasks`, then `Risks`), the new Done items land inside Tasks. Likewise, plans/FORGE-INTAKE-1.md:45 has a section between Done when and Risks. The parser in src/forge/story.py:460–486 stops each section at the next heading, so these additions are excluded from the story's requirements despite handback reporting success.
The same append also places new Change bullets after an existing trailing `Design:` line. src/forge/design.py:101–113 requires that metadata to remain the last line of What changes for you, so extending a previously valid user-facing plan makes its next read fail.
Insert additions inside their actual sections and preserve trailing design metadata. The new regression test only joins freshly generated plans, so neither established-plan case is covered.

stop.reason: Harm 3 defect: the joined text lands in the wrong section, so one more round fixes it

why: Handing back an intake as a plan with a story key that already has a branch prints a raw git worktree error and points to forge doctor, although the intake is used (issue 1388)
